content:
Keeping medicines topped up takes planning when getting out is hard.

This guide covers practical ways to manage repeats. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Ordering

  • NHS App or online services.
  • Your GP practice.
  • Some pharmacies can manage requests for you.

Collection and delivery

Ask your pharmacy whether delivery is available in your area.

Packaging for stiff hands

  • Ask for easy-open caps.
  • Ask about blister packs or other aids if you struggle.

Medicines reviews

Ask your GP or pharmacist to review your medicines, especially if you take several.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can someone order for me?

Yes, with proxy access or your permission.

Is delivery free?

It depends on the pharmacy.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: The NHS App
